questions: How many NbSe2/CrBr3 devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed a zero-field diode effect? The text names devices #1, #2 and #3.
Why were the others set aside, and how did you choose device #1 for Figs. 1, 2 and 3(b) and device #3 for Fig. 3(a)?
Which ranges of temperature, field (sweep amplitude and training field) and current did you measure beyond those shown, and what training field preceded the -35.7% value in Fig. 2?
What does the second-best device look like? Could device #2's field sweeps, with its Bcf and Bcb, move from the SM into the main text?

How did you fix zero applied field after the ±50 mT sweeps and the ±6 T training? A superconducting magnet can leave a remanent field of order 10 mT, the scale of your Bcf and Bcb; was a Hall sensor or reference sample measured alongside?
Did you measure a bare NbSe2 flake, or a part of the same flake without CrBr3, with the same geometry and field history, and how do the diode effect and its field dependence compare?

Was the training field applied with NbSe2 superconducting? If you set the CrBr3 state above the NbSe2 Tc (and below the CrBr3 ordering temperature) and then cool in zero field, does the zero-field polarity still follow the CrBr3 state?
Were the RMCD loops in the SM taken on the transport devices themselves and at what temperature, so that B0 and Bco can be compared with Bcf and Bcb of the same flake?
